### 2026-10-01 — # I actually made a font renderer

**5.2h**

# I actually made a font renderer
> TL;DR: Developed a simple dot-style font rendering and used it on an OLED using an Arduino UNO.

So first I started by testing a old 2.4" TFT screen I had lying around, but after looking into datasheets (for the IC that it uses) and some wiring diagrams, I found out it was broken since I connected it directly instead of using resistors :).

![IMG_1005](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/7a581182ba35333f29f435f6a018fcced654ef76d024bec2980a88d55ea529a9.png)

So I just decided to use an OLED for prototyping instead. So I first started by wiring it to an Arduino UNO.

![IMG_1002](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/3984c52f657b4e9ca546232a0592c8ea1d1f53379f0b5d1e7b1b3a8d6f4c53da.png)

Then writing a simple sketch to just initialize the OLED (and it worked *_*).

![Screenshot_20261001_203648](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/4060a108d15590e998cac98467f1cf1be9d1f7197bd4cc91ce8b3f7654143850.png)

So next I needed to make like a simple font renderer for the font style I wanted. After a while of just researching and trying to know how other people did it, I found that there is a list for font styles (font lookup table). And I used one that seemed appropriate, and after that all I had to do Is draw circles at the positions of each pixel entry. Although I did have issues with the list not being in memory and I had to add it to PROGMEM (program memory) which stored it internally (in the arduino UNO).

![Screenshot_20261001_203656](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/464860383cc225cf32982488f95fafac1cf4f75c31dca941fdc1e591cc977867.png)

Next, I also added some custom glyphs and Icons for the future to display like the degree and celcius, etc.

![Screenshot_20261001_203709](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/5046bde17c340d690d9f683a6a9061bbfa208a572c669e104856a3449f9f5a41.png)

Then after I got that working I had to basically add it to the main sketch, but that also raised issues because I put font_renderer.c instead of the expected font_renderer.cpp and that was a simple fix (since I had encountered this issue before). And it was basically working and correctly compiling.

![Screenshot_20261001_214802](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/f1bc88c4dcd2af4ffc4960b49873f9abbb464852e5c9685ec91bc818ecd06721.png)

![IMG_1004](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/32dfd77f6dc254bebe128d4ea62ced26f3808e45c9397f6fc2435e02a56aad9b.png)

Then I started working on the actual project repo (on [github](https://github.com/rayvn-42/AirClock).) I first started by writing a simple README file, I added things like the reason for this project and what it is, but its still missing pictures for the 3D design, Schematic and more since those will be added in the future.

![Screenshot_20261001_223708](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/be7ef146105ac4011311f631d2b4fe289acdd5eeb6208095c13c30d1f1fcd81a.png)

And then finallyyy once that was done I pushed everything to github.

![Screenshot_20261001_232105](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/860ab3877f28bbc621e297a81dc005a52263dfebec716f7e75c7e8dd001ca383.png)

**Next things I'll work on**:  are probably porting the code to ESP32 then adding the actual data display part. Also design a 3D model for the case, and the schematics and probably the PCB board too.

### 2026-10-02 — ## The cable is broken :/

**5.1h**

## The cable is broken :/
> TL;DR: I ported the arduino UNO code to ESP32 and added  a weather API and a WiFi Manager.
---
So I first started by just reading an [article](https://medium.com/@ceavinrufus/using-ssd1306-oled-display-on-esp32-bonus-project-b9157dc0d06d) on using an oled display with an ESP32, and it turned out that its basically same code as an Arduino UNO.

![Screenshot_20261002_135842](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/044f0a8be1a03b8bb72644fe1fe7bd4a0a1acfdeda7162372dd3322c4f1d4b60.png)

So I just uploaded that same code to the ESP32. And it ran fine and rendered the text just like the Arduino UNO.

![IMG_1006](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/928c3afae54b7de3b08922afae1bee3ee2c76528fb410ae8d6938261d108cbd2.png)

Once that worked fine, I wanted to add a weather api, so I searched for a free  one that didn't need a key and found [open-meteo](https://open-meteo.com) and it looks like it has a lot of data. And like its a perfect fit, so I just decided to go with it. I read some of the Documentation and it seemed quite easy to use too.

![Screenshot_20261002_141041](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/6affff2b01a6c681864bdd02b6e8a3b209576618e587c23b2483c87feba5e30e.png)

But then I realized that I need to be connected to a WiFi router, but hardcoding it is bad practice and not really accessible for the user. So I decided to use a WifiManager, it basically starts the ESP32 in AP mode and hosts it own webpage where the user can enter his info. Once that's done it switches back to client mode and connects to that AP. Once that was complete I also implemented a few more functions such as `showOledMessage` and `GetWeather` just as wrappers or helper functions.

![Screenshot_20261002_143717](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/6f7e31579495df1661ffc709e7076ccb02c6183933690abc173f9b78297039bf.png)

Then basically added some more nice comments. And compile.

![Screenshot_20261002_151557](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/f49fbb86e08a36e7eb405d35def26493844f8ced1666844b6368842cb48dbc48.png)

Once it compiled I plugged in the ESP32 and decided to Upload. But it kept crashing, and getting stuck in a reboot loop (due to the `Esp.restart()`). And after searching a bit why this might be, I discovered that the cable I was using was just too weak to handle the load, and kept cutting off.

![Screenshot_20261002_152517](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/6bc5a9782d5474acd097bd470b620a8123fe78bff0cfd174ffe0301dd0ca43df.png)

The bad cable :(

![IMG_1007](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/XoBihhfZo6FAvvRPA5lxGMbSZAmBagkB/5a99235501fc655e65e10c311dafba6d7fb9c09a1c4898853f17540394c5e24e.png)

So now I need to buy a new cable to continue development :).
